extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed final mechanism framing from reopened XML/PDF/supplement/Data S1; not an unreviewed automated locator note.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: F6P1/F6P6 directly damage C. perfringens cell envelope integrity, with NPN, PI uptake, DiSC3-5 depolarization, TEM, and CLSM used as source assays; F6P6 is framed as stronger capsule/cell-wall damage while F6P1 is framed as stronger membrane-disruption/rapid killing at comparable concentration.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: F6P1 and F6P6 hybrid antimicrobial peptides
mechanism_claims.limitations: Mechanism is direct envelope-disruption evidence for C. perfringens; no single specific protein target is established by pull-down.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: HAMPs show biofilm inhibition/clearing context and concentration-dependent self-assembly/agglutination; this is phenotype/mechanism-support evidence rather than a separate molecular target.

source_locator.locator: xml:fig=4; supplementary_pdf:fig. S6, fig. S7, fig. S12

mechanism_claims.limitations: Bacterial aggregation/self-assembly supports delivery/action context but is not normalized as an MIC endpoint.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: In mouse C. perfringens infection models, HAMPs and EPV@HAMPs reduce bacterial burden and inflammatory/toxin readouts; this is in vivo efficacy and downstream disease-context evidence, not proof of direct immune modulation independent of bacterial reduction.
mechanism_claims.limitations: The review does not promote reduced inflammatory readouts to a direct anti-inflammatory mechanism; the paper itself states this limitation.
